The turbine had a chord-to-radius ratio (c/R) of 0.49.
The chord length (c) of the blades was 4.06 cm, the span (h) was 23.4 cm, and the preset pitch angle (αp) was -6°.
The turbine radius to the quarter chord (R) was 8.23 cm.
The Reynolds number based on chord and freestream was 44,000.
The Froude numbers based on water depth (H) and submergence (S) were 0.37 and 0.67, respectively.
The turbine blockage ratio (β) was 9.3%, and the solidity (σ) was 0.16 for the two-bladed configuration and 0.08 for the single-bladed configuration.
The positively cambered blades exhibited sub-optimal performance compared to the symmetrical blades.
The negatively cambered blades slightly improved on the symmetrical blade performance by enhancing downstream flow reattachment.
The negatively cambered blades reduced peak loading by 13% compared to the symmetrical blades.
The optimal tip-speed ratio (λ) decreased slightly with increased camber, from 2.15 for the negatively cambered blades to 1.98 for the positively cambered blades.
The researchers used the method of Migliore and Wolfe to estimate the virtual camber and incidence of the blades.
The virtual camber of the symmetrical NACA 0018 foil was estimated to be 6% at infinite tip-speed ratio (λ=∞).
The position of maximum virtual camber was approximately 0.49c for the c/R=0.49 turbine.
The virtual incidence (αi) was estimated to be 7° for the c/R=0.49 turbine, opposing the preset pitch of -6°.
The study found that the influence of geometric camber is non-linear, and that using a simplistic summation of geometric and virtual camber may be overly simplistic.
